source.locator: arXiv:2405.00118v3, Lemma 5 in the proof of Theorem 2, main.tex lines 1539--1560; construction in Appendix D.2, lines 4098--4162
source.verbatim_statement: There exists constants \(c,c'>0\) such that for any constants \(c_1,c_2,c_3>0\) satisfying \(cc_1c_3/c_2^2\leq 1\) and \(d\leq c_3n\log n\), there exist two distributions \(\mu_0\) and \(\mu_1\) on \((p,\pi,\mu)\) satisfying: \(0\leq p\leq c_1\log n/n\), \(\epsilon\leq\pi\leq1-\epsilon\), and \(0\leq\mu\leq1\) almost surely; with \(K=c_2\log n\), \(E_{\mu_0}[p^i(p\pi)^j(p\pi\mu)^k]=E_{\mu_1}[p^i(p\pi)^j(p\pi\mu)^k]\) for nonnegative \(i,j,k\) satisfying \(i+j+k\leq3K\); \(a_0:=E_{\mu_0}[p]=E_{\mu_1}[p]\leq1/d\); and \(|E_{\mu_0}[p\mu]-E_{\mu_1}[p\mu]|\geq c_4/(n\log n)\), where \(c_4=cc'c_1/c_2^2\).

added_lemmas.justification: These matched triple moments are the published substrate for the rare-cell count-mixture construction.
added_lemmas.gap: The cited lemma supplies approximate-mass priors, not exact fixed-sample probability-law priors; the consumer theorem proves the confidence-interval de-Poissonization separately.
added_lemmas.consumer: The rare-cell component of the honest confidence-length converse.

proposed_statement_changes.reason: The current witness claim is stronger than the cited source: its rare-cell priors live on approximate mass vectors in a Poisson experiment, and the published normalization lemma transfers only squared risk, not fixed-n predictive total variation. The proposed claim retains and proves the full same-class confidence-length lower frontier through an explicit interval-level randomized-sample-size de-Poissonization, while making no unsupported assertion that the normalized rare priors themselves form a close exact fixed-n pair.

proposed.justification: This certifies the full confidence-width lower frontier in the identical raw conditional fourth-central-moment class used by the interval.
proposed.gap: ZengBalakrishnanHanKennedy2024, Theorem 2 and Appendix C.5, lower-bound squared-error risk for the one-arm functional \(\psi_1\). Its approximate-mass Poisson priors do not themselves give an exact fixed-n confidence-length pair; the present theorem instead proves an interval-level de-Poissonization that transfers their direct testing separation.
proposed.consumer: The minimax optimality certificate for the robust interval and a diagnostic showing why shorter 401(k) intervals cannot be uniformly honest without added structure.

proposed_core_edits.reason: Synchronize the theorem's dependency and symbol metadata with the narrowed, proved interval-level de-Poissonization claim and its cited moment-matching substrate.
